title: A Lexically Filtered Meron-Cluster Benchmark: Exact Ground Truth, Mechanized Cancellation Lemmas, and a Pilot That Exposes Answer Leakage
description: This deposit contains a small, exactly solvable instance of the meron-cluster mechanism for the fermion sign problem, machine-checked lemmas for it, and the record of a pilot language-model run that cannot support a discovery claim. The instance is a four-site periodic chain with 256 breakup graphs and 1,296 configurations, 192 of them negative. An exact oracle, written with SQLite and rational arithmetic, finds that the 57 graphs containing a meron cluster cancel exactly and that the other 199 give the signed sum Z = 912; an independent transfer-matrix trace also gives 912. Lean 4 proofs cover the per-orbit cancellation lemmas. A substring filter and five prompt builders present the instance as a graph problem without twelve domain words. In the retained pilot, five language models were accessed through OpenRouter with one run per model and prompt type, and no unassisted prompt produced a passing answer (0 of 9). Every pass came after the prompt contained the answer: the scorer's feedback states that Z must equal 912 and gives the split into 57 cancelling and 199 surviving subgraphs, and one prompt type also dictates the sign formula and the cancellation step. Even the unassisted prompts state the configuration count and the average sign, which fix Z. The paper describes the changes a valid rerun needs; that rerun requires authorized live API calls and has not been made.
